text:
Sam: Heads-up — saw a ~35% uptick in job failures last night for preemptible pools in us-west1. P99 spikes, a lot of restarts. Anyone else seeing this?
Anya: Yup, noticed interruptions around 02:14–02:22 PST. capacity-bot fired a bunch of reclaim alerts.
capacity-bot: market_volatility=high region=us-west1 reclaimed=23 nodes at 2026-03-18T02:16:09Z
Jin: Do we know if this is price churn or actual capacity shortage?
Mike: Looks like capacity churn. Spot-price stayed flat but availability dropped. GCE showed preemptible quota pressure.
Eva: Can we switch the critical inference pools to capacity-optimized instead of price-optimized? That reduced evictions for a customer last month.
Sam: Curious about trade-offs — cost vs availability. If we move all GPU pools to capacity-optimized our avg hourly cost might tick up a bit. But job success rate improves.
Anya: Proposal: 2-tier mix. Critical real-time routes -> capacity-optimized + 10% warm buffer. Batch training -> price-optimized with aggressive retry/backoff.
Jin: Agree. Also add jitter on scale-up so we don't bring up hundreds of nodes simultaneously and get a correlated reclaim. Something like random(5s..30s) between node requests.
Mike: +1 on jitter. Also recommend soft-eviction handler so in-flight KV/cache can flush before kill. We have a small hook already:
```
# preempt hook example
curl -X POST $OP_ENDPOINT/evict -d '{"node":"$HOSTNAME","deadline":120}'
# returns: allow_graceful_shutdown=true
```
But need wider rollout.
Eva: And a warm pool: keep N GPUs idle (or low-util) per region to absorb churn. N = max(1, floor(cluster_gpu_count * 0.08)).
Sam: How about autoscaler config? Anyone tested mixing allocation strategies in the same managed group? We use multi-pool: one capacity-optimized group + one price-optimized for overflow.
Anya: That pattern worked. Overflow pool should have a scaling cooldown and longer termination grace period. Also set node selectors so critical pods avoid overflow group.
Jin: Ops note: monitor preemption rate (%) and mean time to replacement. Add alert if preemption_rate_5m > 2% or mttr > 3m.
Mike: Terraform snippet for AWS spot (for reference):
```
resource "aws_launch_template" "gpu" {
  # ...
  instance_market_options {
    market_type = "spot"
    spot_options {
      allocation_strategy = "capacity-optimized"
      instance_interruption_behavior = "terminate"
      max_price = "0.60"
    }
  }
}
```
Adapt for GCP by using `preemptible = true` and relying on zone selection for capacity.
Eva: Also consider proactive region-failover: keep a small standby group in us-central with cross-region routing. If us-west1 spikes, we can route a % of traffic to standby.
Sam: Cost ask: what's expected delta if we move 3 critical pools to capacity-optimized + 10% warm buffer? Rough calc: ~+12% GPU-hours, but job success improves and less wasted retries. Worth it for SLA-sensitive customers.
Anya: I'll run a quick sim against last 30 days' reclaim trace and post numbers.
Jin: Small infra TODOs: 1) add jitter to scale-up (PR) 2) enable preempt hook on gpu node image 3) add warm-buffer param to autoscaler 4) create alert thresholds.
Mike: I can do the terraform change for one pool and smoke test in staging today.
Eva: If staging looks good we flip one production shard and monitor 24h.
Sam: Nice. @Anya can you open the sim PR and tag me? I'll pair with @Mike on the infra change. :thumbsup:
Anya: On it. Opening PR in a few hours.
capacity-bot: created_incident=INC-2026-1146 linked_runbook=https://redwood.internal/runbooks/spot-eviction-playbook
Sam: Great — let's target rolling this week. If anyone sees a worse regression after the flip, rollback plan is to revert allocation_strategy and re-enable price-optimized.
Mike: Will do. Planning to add 30s randomized startup delay and the preempt hook as part of the change.
Eva: Also adding a dashboard tile: preemptions, replacement latency, cost uplift, and batch failure rate.
Sam: Cool. Thanks all.
Anya: PR: https://git.redwood/repo/infra/pulls/789 — draft with sim results will follow.
